models.title: Domestic-currency risk of a risk-free foreign asset
models.summary: When the foreign asset is risk-free, domestic-currency return risk is the gross foreign return scaling the exchange-rate volatility.

relationship.original_equation: sigma(RDC) = (1 + RFC) x sigma(RFX) for sigma(RFC) = 0 (Nguyen results A/B)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM3 Nguyen example results A/B, printed pp. 196-197 (PDF pp. 204-205): with risk-free foreign assets, expected domestic-currency risk is (1.04) x 8% = 8.3% (Australia) and (1.06) x 10% = 10.6% (New Zealand)
relationship.translation_notes: Decimals. Exact (not approximate) because the asset leg has zero variance. Specialization of Eq5 with sigma(RFC) = 0.

variables.definition: Standard deviation of exchange-rate moves, decimal
Standard deviation of domestic-currency return, decimal

assumptions: Foreign-currency asset return known (risk-free); FX volatility estimated.
limitations: Risk-free-asset case only; risky assets need the full variance decomposition (sibling record).

models.title: Two-asset domestic-currency return variance
models.summary: Variance of domestic-currency return for two foreign assets as weighted variances plus the correlation term (exact form for risk-free legs).

relationship.original_equation: s2(RDC) = w1^2 s2(R1) + w2^2 s2(R2) + 2 w1 w2 s(R1) s(R2) rho(R1,R2) (Eq4, risk-free-asset application)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM3 two-asset domestic variance Eq4, printed pp. 196-197 (PDF pp. 204-205), Nguyen example: equally weighted s2 = (0.5)2(8.3%)2+(0.5)2(10.6%)2+2(0.5)(0.5)(8.3%)(10.6%)(0.85) = 0.8%; long-short (w = -1/+1) s2 = 0.3%
relationship.translation_notes: Decimals. Inputs s1/s2 are standard deviations; v1/v2 their squares as stated. Negative weights allowed (long-short).
